text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — canary for raven-int8 on canary-pool showing weird action-invocation parse failures when we expect strict JSON. baseline (raven-fp16) ~0.3% failures, int8 canary at 2.1% over 10k calls. :eyes:

emily: Ugh. Any pattern by prompt type or prefix length?

sanjay: Mostly multi-step tool sequences that include a 1k token system + 300 token user history. Failures are JSON parse errors — truncated/garbled trailing braces or stray text after JSON. Not typical hallucinations, more like cut-off or tokenization noise.

mike: Could be kv-cache + batching causing mid-output truncation when streaming? What's batch size and kv_cache setting for canary?

sanjay: Canary config: `batch_target_tokens=2048`, `max_batch=8`, `kv_cache=true`, `streaming=true`. Canary workload uses prefix_history=true (we keep user+assistant history in prefix).

olivia: Can you paste an example of the raw model output (exact bytes we received) for one failure?

sanjay: Sure — one failing response below (copied from logs):

```
Request prompt: {system: ..., user: "Explain steps and return tool call in JSON"}
Model stream chunk 1: "assistant: {\n  \"action\": {\n    \"name\": \"search\",\n    \"args\": {\n      \"q\": \"redwood inference kv cache\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"meta\": {\n    \"step\": 1"\n"
Model stream chunk 2: "\n}\n}Some extra text about results"
```

Note: chunk2 appended an extra human-readable sentence after the closing brace. That breaks our strict JSON parser.

jordan: Interesting — not a truncation per se, but extra trailing text. That suggests the model completed a JSON token then continued with commentary. Maybe quantization changed pattern near end-of-output probability mass, so it sometimes emits an extra tail.

emily: How often is it extra-text vs truncated? We need signal breakdown.

sanjay: Breakdown from canary telemetry: out of 10k calls: 76 had extra-tail text (0.76%), 132 had truncated/garbled endings (1.32%), rest were fine. Combined parse-fail 2.08% (rounded to 2.1%). FP16 baseline combined parse-fail was 0.31%.

mike: Do we see any difference when streaming is off (non-streaming response)?

sanjay: Ran a small AB: streaming=false reduced extra-tail to 0.1% but truncated still at ~1.2%. So streaming interacts but isn't the whole story.

olivia: My gut: quantization changed logits around EOS & punctuation tokens; when we have long prefix (KV cache) the model's distribution for final tokens diverges occasionally and it produces non-json commentary after the JSON block. Two mitigations: 1) enforce post-output truncation at first closing brace + strict JSON extractor, 2) soft prompt-suffix that nudges explicit end marker like `
<<END_JSON>>`.

jordan: Another option: a small decoder-side heuristic to stop generation once the JSON parse becomes valid + next token probability for `
`/`}` is low. But that needs runtime integration.

devex-bot: Telemetry rule suggestion: tag canary runs with `quantization=int8` + `kv_prefix=true` + `streaming=true` so we can slice.

mike: For experiments: can we run mirrored replay with fp16 and int8 with identical non-streaming config + same random seed? Also try disabling kv_cache.

sanjay: I'll queue mirrored jobs: 50k calls each. Also adding a targeted prompt set with lots of small toolcalls vs long multi-step tool sequences.

emily: For user-facing quick fix, I'd prefer implement a structured-output wrapper in the router: if response appears to begin with JSON, run 1 quick repair attempt: extract first balanced JSON object (greedy closing brace), then if leftover text non-empty do 1 retry with `thought: output must be strict JSON only` and attach the extracted JSON to parse fallback. Keep retry budget small.

olivia: Be careful — greedy balancing can mis-parse nested objects or arrays. Use a counter-based bracket matcher and only accept if top-level parse valid. Also log raw failing output for eval.

ops-bot: Deploy note: a small router patch for extractor+retry will be rolled to canary next deploy window if approved.

jordan: Also validate whether this is model-internal (quant noise) vs runtime (kv concatenation ordering). Suggest token-level logging around boundary tokens for failed examples.

sanjay: Agreed. Plan: 1) mirrored 50k AB (fp16 vs int8) non-streaming + streaming variations; 2) token-boundary debug logging on 1k failing samples; 3) implement router soft-extractor + single retry with `strict-json` hint; 4) re-run canary. I'll post updates here once runs finish.

emily: Thanks — please include evaluation script that computes recall/precision of extractor vs ground-truth JSON so we don't overfit a heuristic.

sanjay: Will do. Assigning follow-ups: @mike run mirrored AB, @jordan enable token-boundary logs, @olivia prototype router-extractor, @emily build extractor eval script.

mike: On it.

olivia: I'll mock patch and run small sim locally first. :face_with_monocle:

jordan: Adding one more thought — try a tiny temperature sweep (0.0, 0.1, 0.2) for int8 to see if lower temp reduces extra-tail. Could be noisier logits at higher temp.

sanjay: Good call. Adding temp sweep to experiments.

emily: Great. Thanks all.

sanjay: Final note: attaching canary tag `canary_run=171945` to all logs for easy querying.
